capabilities.title: verify_card
capabilities.description: Verify a signed gspc.measurement-card under the published rule (https://councilof.ai/signed/HOW-TO-VERIFY.md): recompute the id from the canonical body bytes, then check the Ed25519 signature under the PINNED key published at did:web:csoai.org#card-attestation-1. A card that carries its own key proves only that the file is self-consistent — anyone can alter a body and sign it with a key they just generated — so a signer other than the published key is reported INVALID. Three verdicts, never two: VALID, INVALID (with the reason), or UNCHECKABLE when the check could not be completed — 'could not check' is a different claim from 'forged'. Accepts the card as a JSON object, a JSON string, or a councilof.ai / csoai.org URL. Never a certification.

capabilities.title: verify_inclusion
capabilities.description: Check a sha256 against the live public-root merkle via GET /api/proof?sha=. Three states only: VALID (included), INVALID (not a leaf), UNCHECKABLE (proof endpoint unreachable). Does not claim Ed25519 unless sig_ed25519 is present and checked separately. Never a grade.

capabilities.title: witness_hash
capabilities.description: PAID (x402 or CSOAI LTD invoice). Witness a SHA-256 digest — 'attest what you're shown' — via https://councilof.ai/api/witness: one public.notice leaf (csoai.witness.hash/0.1) in the next hourly signed public root, an RFC-3161 timestamp over the digest, and the root's Rekor + OpenTimestamps anchors. Hash-only: name a digest, or a public URL fetched once (robots honoured, never past a login, paywall or bot check → UNCHECKABLE, nothing charged). Attests existence of the digest at the root's as_of — nothing about content, legality or provenance; a self-signed card carries no legal presumption. Measurement, not certification. Status is free at /api/witness/status. Without x_payment the tool returns the 402 challenge. If the route is not deployed on this origin the tool says NOT_DEPLOYED.
capabilities.availability_reason: /api/witness returns 503 lifecycle=QUARANTINED_PRE_RELEASE. Paid witness issuance is disabled until a release gate verifies atomic leaf -> signed root -> exact-byte sidecar -> Rekor snapshot -> OpenTimestamps chain. Declared so the contract is stable; deliberately not served.

mcp_detail.note: declared and served differ on purpose. A capability may be declared so its contract is stable while its runtime is deliberately gated. Any OTHER difference is drift and capabilities/registry.test.mjs fails closed on it.

availability_vocabulary.VERIFIED: observed working at runtime on this transport
availability_vocabulary.LOCAL_CANDIDATE: works locally; no production host round trip proven
availability_vocabulary.OWNER_GATED: implemented and deliberately disabled pending a named gate
availability_vocabulary.UNAVAILABLE: declared but not served, and not deliberately gated — this is drift

availability_scope_note: Only MCP-declared capabilities carry an availability state. The other 72 HTTP/A2A entries are UNASSESSED and deliberately left without a field rather than given a fabricated one.

transport_availability.method: direct HTTP probe of each endpoint; states use the same five-value vocabulary as the MCP capabilities above

agui.reason: GET /api/agui/gspc-state returns 200 and emits real STATE_DELTA / TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT SSE derived from /api/gspc. PRESENTATION ONLY — an AG-UI event never advances MEASURED, SIGNED or WITNESSED, and EOF is not a run completing.

agui_wire.reason: GET /api/agui/wire returns 503 agui_wire_unconfigured. The general provider wire needs AGUI_WIRE_URL set; until then the central client consumes no AG-UI stream.

a2a_discovery.reason: GET /.well-known/agent-card.json returns 200, protocolVersion 1.0.0, 5 skills, 2 supportedInterfaces. DISCOVERY ONLY.

a2a_tasks.reason: GET /api/a2a/key and /api/a2a both return 404. There is no public task send/get/cancel runtime, so the declared card is not backed by an executable A2A surface. Discovery is not a task runtime.

a2ui.reason: GET /api/a2ui returns 404. No renderer endpoint and no proven component round trip, so no A2UI capability is offered on any transport.

transport_availability.note: HTTP is authoritative. MCP exposes tools. AG-UI streams presentation events and cannot advance evidence state. A2A carries discovery today and no task identity. A2UI has no renderer. Nothing here may be described as live beyond its state.

journey_backends.why: WP-3 asks for the case-model journey ask -> scope -> inspect -> explain -> propose -> approve -> fix -> retest -> receipt -> monitor, and says a missing backend must show the EXACT unavailable capability rather than a faked completed fix. These are the endpoints that journey needs. They are recorded here as measured runtime state so the gap is a fact with a date on it, not an assumption carried between handoffs.
journey_backends.client_reference_note: Zero files under client/ reference /api/ras, /api/remediation, /api/jobs or /api/receipts. The product does not fake these: it does not offer them at all. That is the honest state while the backend is absent, and it is asserted so a future surface cannot quietly promise an execute path that still 404s.

ras.reason: GET /api/ras and /api/ras/status both return 404 not_found. There is no remediation-and-scoping runtime behind the journey, so no approve -> fix -> retest cycle can be completed or shown.

remediation.reason: GET /api/remediation returns 404 not_found. Nothing can execute a proposed change, so any UI offering to apply a fix would be describing an action the estate cannot take.

jobs.reason: GET /api/jobs returns 404 not_found. There is no job record, so completed-job counts for WP-6 growth cannot be measured from runtime and must not be estimated.

receipts.reason: GET /api/receipts/latest returns 200 with status UNPUBLISHED, items [] and count 0, and its own note points at csoai-x402-receipt-mcp for the signed receipt lane. The surface answers; it publishes nothing. A journey cannot end in a receipt here.

findings.reason: GET /api/findings returns 200 and carries the CSOAI fleet population with its own schema, honesty block and as_of. This is the one journey input that IS live — inspect and explain can be served from it; propose, fix, retest and receipt cannot.

journey_backends.consequence_for_wp3_and_wp6: Four of the five backends the journey needs are absent or publish nothing. The reachable part of the case model today is ask -> scope -> inspect -> explain, from /api/findings and /api/gspc. Everything from propose onward has no runtime. Building approve/fix/retest/receipt UI over this would be the faked completed fix WP-3 forbids, so it is not built; this block records why and will fail loudly the moment TUI 1 lands the backend.

distributed_artifacts.why: WP-4 lists SDK and plugin among the nine surfaces. This is the one a user installs.

sdk_npm.reason: csoai-gspc-mcp is published on npm at 0.2.1 (4 versions) and the published tarball is BYTE-IDENTICAL to mcp/gspc-server: index.mjs, gspc-tools.json, verify-card.mjs and paid-tools.json all match. This is the SDK/plugin surface a user actually installs. Drift is the default failure here because publishing needs the owner's Bypass-2FA token (the account is WebAuthn, so --otp= can never work), so anyone can change the repo and nobody can republish — guarded by capabilities/npm-package-parity.test.mjs.
